claims.statement: In the pinned packages-inherit-permissions feature scope, FPT and GHEC, a published package linked to a repository inherits repository access and its workflows gain access unless the organization disabled automatic inheritance. This is not a verified organization setting, GHES claim or permission receipt.

Container Registry stores images under an organization or personal account and permits repository association. Permissions may inherit from that repository or be independently granular; public images allow anonymous access. Anonymous public reads do not establish anonymous private access or publication authority.
The supplied enterprise container registry hostname is an illustrative company-domain example, not an owned or verified service endpoint; no connection or credential transmission was made.

The GHES branch describes Container Registry as public preview and subject to change, despite the beta filename. Both GitHub Packages and subdomain isolation must be enabled; the fragment neither proves those prerequisites nor authorizes changing them.

The pinned fragment states that GHES 3.6 supports migration of organization-owned Docker images and describes user-owned migration as future work. This historical statement is not proof of present-version support, completed migration or authorization to migrate; later-release claims require separate reconciliation.
Registry hostname rendering selects ghcr.io for FPT/GHEC and containers.HOSTNAME for GHES. HOSTNAME is unresolved target data, not a real verified domain or permission to authenticate.
